display.purpose: Page title only. One instance per page.

data.purpose: Live price output values. tabular-nums required.

body.purpose: General UI prose, fixed-rate display, slider labels.

label.purpose: Method identifiers and system panel names. Uppercase, tight tracking.

caption.purpose: Meta text, footer, citations, secondary information.

motion.name: link-hover
motion.purpose: Color transition on footer links and citation links. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: chart-transition
motion.purpose: Plotly chart data animation on parameter change. Controlled via clientside_callback in app.py; cannot be overridden by CSS prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Sidebar stacks full-width above cards; cards wrap to 2-column grid.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: All columns stack single-column. Page padding reduces to 16px. Title and price scale down to 1.7rem.

narrative.overview:
The Rigorous Witness observes algorithms without editorializing. It shows what Black-Scholes, Monte Carlo, and Quantum Amplitude Estimation compute — exactly as computed, with their error bars, their timing, their honest limitations. The visual language is a direct extension of the README's intellectual honesty: no gradient implies more than the numbers deliver, no flourish oversells a 600-point precomputed grid as live quantum hardware.

The system is dark because quant researchers work in low ambient light, staring at terminals and notebooks. The background (#0a0e1a) is deep navy with a trace of blue — not arbitrary black, not a generic 'cool dark.' Card surfaces (#111827) lift one tonal step from the background, and hairline white-alpha borders mark container edges without adding visual noise. No shadows. The chart is the depth.

Three method identity colors carry the entire chromatic load: Formula Green for Black-Scholes, Simulation Amber for Monte Carlo, Quantum Indigo for QAE. Outside those three and the structural neutrals, nothing is colored. This system explicitly rejects generic SaaS dashboard aesthetics and the dark-mode cliché of 2024.
keyCharacteristics: Three-color method vocabulary, used exclusively for method identity — never decoration
Flat surfaces, hairline borders, zero shadows — the chart is the only depth
Single sans family (Inter), two weights (800 display / 700 data and labels)
Uppercase text reserved for method identifiers and the parameters panel label only
All numeric displays use tabular-nums for column alignment under changing values

rules.name: The Three Witnesses Rule
rules.body: Formula Green, Simulation Amber, and Quantum Indigo are reserved for method identity. Never repurpose them for hover states, decorative borders, or UI elements that don't directly represent one of the three pricing methods.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Secondary Ink (#9ca3af) is the lightest text color in the system. It must not be made lighter. It passes WCAG AA on both surface tones; #6b7280 — its predecessor — failed at 4.0:1.

rules.name: The Uppercase Restriction Rule
rules.body: Uppercase text appears in exactly two contexts: method name labels on cards and the parameters panel header. Any new uppercase text must identify a named system component — not serve as a section header or decorative eyebrow.

rules.name: The Tabular-Nums Rule
rules.body: Every numeric value that changes at runtime must use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Proportional digits cause layout shift as values animate.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are prohibited on all surfaces. Depth is structural (tonal layering) not cosmetic. Adding box-shadow immediately reads as generic SaaS decoration.

dos: Do use Formula Green, Simulation Amber, and Quantum Indigo exclusively for their respective method contexts.
Do use Secondary Ink (#9ca3af) for all secondary text — labels, metadata, captions.
Do use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on all price outputs and numeric values that animate.
Do keep containers flat: 1px hairline border, no box-shadow.
Do use text-wrap: balance on any headline that could wrap.
Do use transition: color 150ms ease on any link that changes color on hover.
Do cite WCAG AA (4.5:1) as the hard floor for any text color on any surface.
donts: Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient. The title's original gradient was removed because it is theatrical, not honest.
Don't add box-shadow to any card, container, or interactive element. The No-Shadow Rule applies universally.
Don't apply glassmorphism (backdrop-filter, blurred card backgrounds). The system is flat by design.
Don't use colorful metric cards with gradient accents — the 'generic SaaS dashboard' PRODUCT.md names as the primary anti-reference.
Don't use neon glow, ambient Quantum Indigo lighting, or purple gradients.
Don't add uppercase text to any element that isn't a method name or a named system label.
Don't introduce a second typeface. One family with weight contrast reads as precise; two competing sans-serifs read as indecision.
